The Nurse Manager (NM) is the designated first-line supervisory authority and is responsible and accountable for the operation of their assigned units and provides coverage for other NMs as needed.

The NM is responsible and accountable for the direction and supervision of specific orientation, training, development of staff, and evaluation of individual staff performance. They function as a role model, educator, practitioner, and supervisor providing leadership to the team.

They influence care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team to remove barriers and implement new evidence-based cutting-edge programs/processes. The NM engages in professional organizations to enhance leadership and career growth.

They adhere to ethical principles in decision-making, fostering accountability at personal, organizational, and staff levels. They equip staff with tools for culturally competent care and promotes a culture of accountability for high-quality, cost-effective outcomes.

They cultivate alliances across the care continuum, building trust through active listening, engagement, and emotional intelligence. The NM contributes to the development of care delivery models and environmental design, ensuring evidence-based, accessible, affordable, and equitable patient care.

Ensures compliance with accreditation and regulatory standards. Aligns nursing/clinical objectives with organizational strategic outcomes, participating in strategy planning and execution. They promote an inclusive workplace valuing diversity to achieve the organizations vision and mission.

The NM maintains knowledge and ensures compliance with all regulatory and accreditation standards, Directives, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOP). Provides peers with informal constructive feedback for improvement. Supports colleagues and other nurses through knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality nursing care.

Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of healthcare professionals. Contributes professional nursing perspective in discussions with the interdisciplinary team. Partners with others to effect change and produce optimal outcomes.

Evaluates outcomes of evidence-based decisions and practice changes for individuals, groups, and populations. Responsible for the documented outcomes at the program or service level. Program or service level outcomes must be broad and complex and can be demonstrated at any organizational level within a facility.

Physical Requirements: This position requires visual acuity, keen· hearing, clear distinctive speech, and manual dexterity. This position requires potentially long periods of continued walking, standing, stooping, sitting, bending, pulling, and pushing. Transferring patients and objects may be required. Mechanical inpatient lifts are provided.

The incumbent may be exposed to infected patients and contaminated materials and may be required to don protective clothing in isolation situations, operative/invasive procedures, or home settings. The incumbent may occasionally be exposed to patients who are combative secondary to delirium, dementia, or psychiatric disorders.

The Specialty Case Management (CM) Registered Nurse (RN) executes position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches in providing complex patient management. Provides patient management, care coordination, and discharge/disposition planning for inpatient and outpatient settings.

The CM RN assists Veterans, family members, and caregivers with receiving the most appropriate options and services to meet their complex health care needs.

This includes, but is not limited to, acute, chronic, multiple, complex, catastrophic, or life-threatening illnesses; combat stress, residuals of traumatic brain injury; community adjustment; addictions and other health problems. Coordinates care with multiple providers across all levels and sites of care.

The CM RN addresses psychosocial, as well as nursing and medical needs of patients and their families/caregivers, through participation in interdisciplinary patient care management practice. The CM RN also evaluates care and outcomes to ensure timely and appropriate provision of services.

Collaborates in the development, implementation, evaluation, and revision of policies, procedures, and/or guidelines. Demonstrates performance and leadership that is broad enough to improve the care for a group of patients. Provides peers with formal or informal constructive feedback for improvement.

Supports colleagues and other nurses through CM knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality nursing care. Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of health care professionals. Evaluates CM outcomes of evidence based decisions and practice changes for individuals, groups, and populations.

Responsible for the documented CM outcomes at the program or service level. Program or service level outcomes must be broad and complex and can be demonstrated at any organizational level within a facility.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Operations & care coordination - Supports patient care across the health care continuum including inpatient and outpatient operations, including patient flow, appointment management, triage, patient education, monitoring progress toward care goals, and ensuring timely follow-up. - Participates in patient encounters as part of the interdisciplinary team to help establish and support patient goals of care. - Uses the nursing process to develop, implement, and evaluate individualized care plans in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team. - Collaborates closely with the interdisciplinary team to coordinate outpatient treatment plans and support treatment planning decisions. - Uses a team-based approach to triage and resolve patient care concerns. - Operates within a dynamic clinical environment requiring consistent physical presence to facilitate timely care coordination, direct patient assessment, and real-time team collaboration.

Must demonstrate adaptability and the ability to provide cross-coverage across units or service lines in response to fluctuating patient volumes, staffing needs, or organizational priorities. - Maintains baseline clinic nurse competency to provide basic clinical coverage when needed to meet operational needs - including patient check-in, routine triage calls, and general patient education - during short-term absences of clinic-based RN staff, consistent with individual competency and scope of practice.

Provider & consult support - Provides daily support to providers by coordinating care with community and VA facilities, ensuring necessary records, test results, and information are available for timely consultations and treatment planning. - Ensures consults are received, reviewed, and appropriately managed (including scheduling, completing e-consults, or discontinuing as appropriate) and works with clinic staff to expedite new patient consults when medically indicated.

Patient communication & access - Communicates with patients about their health care options within the VA and community, following eligibility guidelines and national directives. - Works with VA Medical Centers, contracted partners, and community facilities to address barriers to accessing needed services.

Strives to provide a positive patient experience through navigation of the health care system to ensure care needs are met. ***Continued in the Education Section.

Major components of this function include surveillance, prevention and control activities; reporting communicable illnesses; infection control policy development; administrative functions; infection control education and training; consultative services, and analysis of infection control data.

The Infection Preventionist (IP) has the authority to function in all services of the organization to coordinate, establish and monitor acceptable infection control practices and standards.

S/he serves as a principal member of the Infection Control Committee and recommends new or revised practices, based on currently accepted evidence-based infection prevention and control strategies.

The IP evaluates clinical parameters to determine the presence of infection, assess the severity of disease, identify specific risk factors, and determine source(s) for infection that can be improved.

The IP analyzes surveillance data monthly, quarterly, and annually to identify unusual occurrences, clusters of infection, infection due to unusual pathogens, and occurrence of healthcare-acquired infections that exceed the targets established for the organization, determining the need for intervention.

The IP uses standard definitions for the identification and classification of events, indicators, or outcomes and appropriate statistical techniques to describe the data, calculate rates and critically evaluate the significance of findings.

The IP analyzes data using comparative data when available and reports epidemiologically significant findings appropriately. The IP evaluates infectiousness of patients and employees with communicable diseases, makes recommendations for isolation or work restrictions, and investigates exposures to these diseases.

The IP recognizes deviations from infection control standards and makes recommendations as necessary to maintain the same level of infection control prevention and control standards throughout all areas of the organization.

The IP evaluates the effectiveness of infection prevention and control measures in assigned areas of responsibility and identifies potential infection hazards and deviations from expected hospital target for infection and/or colonization of patients.

The IP facilitates implementation of infection control policies and procedures and makes recommendations for integration of infection control principles throughout the medical center. The IP monitors implementation of infection control policies and procedures.

The IP identifies opportunities to integrate surveillance findings into the organization's plan for improvement and initiates and facilitates procedural changes to improve infection control practices through active participation and/or collaboration with appropriate committees or workgroups.

The IP takes remedial action and implements immediate infection control measures when a known breach is identified or there is reason to believe that there is danger of exposure to or spread of infection in patients or personnel. The IP communicates and follows up with all services involved to ensure corrective action is implemented.

The IP formulates individual goals for specific areas of individual responsibility to accomplish the broader goals of the Infection Control Program. The IP participates in Quality Improvement activities and contributes epidemiological skills and expert knowledge of infection prevention and control methods.

The IP uses knowledge of current scientific literature and existing regulations and guidelines to incorporate appropriate recommendations into written infection control policies and procedures and to ensure consistency with current standards of care.

The IP establishes and maintains effective oral and written communications with all services and community agencies as needed concerning prevention and control of infections in patients. The IP ensures that findings, recommendations, and policies of the infection control program are disseminated to appropriate individuals.
